Package de.labathome.trustconstr.records

Class OptimizeResult

java.lang.Object
de.labathome.trustconstr.records.OptimizeResult
public class OptimizeResult extends Object
Mutable output of MinimizeTrustConstr.minimize(java.util.function.Function<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, java.lang.Double>, java.util.function.Function<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix>, java.util.function.Function<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix>, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, C, int, double, double). Mirrors scipy's OptimizeResult: the solution, KKT-related residuals, iteration counters, termination metadata, and constraint multipliers.

    • status

      public int status
      {0, 1, 2, 3}: Termination status: 0 : The maximum number of function evaluations is exceeded. 1 : `gtol` termination condition is satisfied. 2 : `xtol` termination condition is satisfied. 3 : `callback` function requested termination.

    • success

      public boolean success
      Whether the optimizer reports success.

      Derived at result construction:

      • status == 1 (gtol satisfied): always true -- gtol-termination requires the constraint violation to also be below gtol.
      • status == 2 (xtol satisfied / trust-radius collapse): true only if the residual constraint violation is below gtol -- distinguishes "converged at an active boundary" from "stuck on an infeasible problem".
      • status == 0 (maxIter exceeded) or status == 3 (callback terminated): false.

      Mirrors scipy's OptimizeResult.success semantics, including the behaviour exercised by scipy test_issue_18882 where a degenerate constraint causes trust-radius collapse with a non-trivial constraint violation -- that outcome reports success=false.
